entries.title: ADR, Yogendra Yadav, Mahua Moitra challenge Bihar SIR in Supreme Court
entries.summary: Association for Democratic Reforms, Yogendra Singh Yadav, Manoj Jha, Mahua Moitra and the People's Union for Civil Liberties petitioned the Supreme Court within days of the Commission's 24 June 2025 order starting a Special Intensive Revision of Bihar's electoral rolls, arguing the exercise risked mass, arbitrary disenfranchisement. The Court heard the case on an expedited basis through July 2025 to January 2026 and reserved judgment on 29 January 2026, delivering a unanimous verdict on 27 May 2026 that upheld the SIR and traced the Commission's power to it to Section 21(3) of the Representation of the People Act, 1950, while issuing directions on Aadhaar as an identity document, disclosure of 'logical discrepancy' lists and other procedural safeguards.

entries.title: West Bengal SIR litigation: Mostari Banu, Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury and others v ECI
entries.summary: After the Commission ordered a Special Intensive Revision of West Bengal's electoral rolls, a group of connected petitions - led by Mostari Banu and later including Congress MP Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury and others - came before the same Supreme Court bench that decided the Bihar SIR case. The matter has stayed open through 2026 as an ongoing supervisory proceeding: the Court has directed deployment of judicial officers (including retired judges) to adjudicate claims and objections, protected those officers, and repeatedly sought Commission data on the huge backlog of appeals before the appellate tribunals it ordered set up.

entries.title: ADR v ECI: challenge to EVM reliability and demand for full VVPAT verification
entries.summary: Association for Democratic Reforms petitioned the Supreme Court seeking a return to paper ballots or, alternatively, verification of every VVPAT slip against EVM counts. On 26 April 2024 a two-judge bench rejected both demands, holding there was no credible evidence of EVM manipulation and that 5% randomised VVPAT verification with administrative safeguards was adequate, while directing that symbol-loading units be sealed for 45 days after results and allowing the second- and third-placed candidates to request a burnt-memory check of 5% of EVMs per assembly segment. Related petitions making the same demand were rejected days later, and a review petition against the judgment was dismissed on 30 July 2024.

entries.title: Mahua Moitra and ADR v ECI: disclosure of Form 17C turnout data
entries.summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra's 2019 writ petition over discrepancies in provisional and final voter-turnout figures remained pending in the Supreme Court; ADR filed an interim application in it during the 2024 general election seeking real-time, polling-station-wise publication of Form 17C. The Commission opposed disclosure, citing the absence of a legal mandate and risk of morphed images undermining public trust. A vacation bench declined interim relief on 24 May 2024, holding that granting it would effectively decide Moitra's main petition, and relisted the case after the vacation; no record of the main petition's final disposal was found.

entries.title: Jaya Thakur and others v Union of India: challenge to the 2023 selection-law Act
entries.summary: A group of connected petitions led by Dr Jaya Thakur challenge Sections 6, 7 and 8 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, arguing it dilutes the Supreme Court's Anoop Baranwal judgment by giving the executive a majority on the selection committee. The case has moved through repeated listings, adjournments and a recusal since January 2024 without a final hearing on merits. On 23 September 2026 a split opinion sent the question of whether it needs a larger bench to the Chief Justice, who is being asked to consider constituting a Constitution Bench.

entries.title: Supreme Court directs West Bengal to ensure officers report for SIR duty
entries.summary: In the West Bengal SIR proceedings, the Supreme Court directed the State to ensure that officers assigned to the Commission for the Special Intensive Revision actually report for duty, after complaints of officers not showing up. This order preceded, and set up, the Court's fuller 20 February 2026 direction deploying judicial officers including retired judges.

entries.title: Supreme Court says it cannot fix a timeline for SIR appellate tribunals
entries.summary: Hearing Adhir Ranjan Chowdhury's plea over the roughly 34 lakh voters deleted in West Bengal's SIR, the Supreme Court said it could not fix a deadline for the appellate tribunals to decide appeals, though it would monitor their functioning, and directed the Commission to produce data on disposal rates. Justice Bagchi noted that at current rates the backlog would take about 21 years to clear. The case was adjourned to 25 August 2026.

entries.title: Supreme Court weighs whether SIR deletions exceeding poll margins matter
entries.summary: On a Trinamool Congress claim that in 31 constituencies the number of voters deleted in the SIR exceeded the winning margin, the Chief Justice asked aloud whether the Court could direct fresh elections on that basis. Justice Bagchi said the point could become relevant if an election result itself came to be decided by the Court. The bench directed that all pending appeals, not only those in the 31 flagged constituencies, be examined.

gaps: The Supreme Court's 9 February 2026 order directing West Bengal to ensure officers report for SIR duty is known only from a passing mention inside reporting on the later 20 February order; its own bench, case number and full text were not independently found. Someone with access to sci.gov.in's order list for W.P.(C) 1089/2025 should pull the primary order.

Mahua Moitra's 2019 Form 17C petition (W.P.(C) 1382/2019) has no confirmed final disposition after the Supreme Court's 24 May 2024 order relisting it post-vacation; neither this research nor the existing elections-2019-2024.json entries found a later hearing or order. Someone should check the Supreme Court's case-status portal directly for W.P.(C) 1382/2019.

Several individual West Bengal SIR grievance petitions before the Supreme Court were not researched as separate matters: a plea about denial of rations after SIR exclusion (which the Court told the petitioner to take to the Calcutta High Court), Congress leader Prasenjit Bose's application for voter deletion/addition data, a case involving a person deported to Bangladesh after an SIR deletion, and a plea over an excluded elderly lawyer. These may be worth their own entries if the section expands its West Bengal SIR coverage.

No dedicated Patna High Court or Calcutta High Court case (as distinct from the Supreme Court's supervisory jurisdiction) about the Commission's conduct was located in this pass; it is possible such petitions exist and were transferred to, or overtaken by, the Supreme Court proceedings, but that was not confirmed.

The exact case number and bench for the 2 April 2026 central-forces order and the 7 May 2026 Sivagnanam resignation were not stated in the sources found; both are filed here under the general West Bengal SIR case number for lack of a more specific one.
